What you need to capture

What the app shows you.

Sign in with Apple or an email link, practise on one small room, then read the phone check before you send anything.

Screens from the current build in the iOS Simulator; on a real iPhone the camera fills the capture screen. The app is in invite-only testing through TestFlight.

One space, five steps.

  1. Choose the space and scope.

    Decide the rooms, private areas to exclude and who reviews. One new accepted capture uses one walkthrough, regardless of room count, and each capture has its own link and QR code. A home with more rooms than fit in one capture takes more captures. Keep street addresses and access instructions out of anything you share.

  2. Prepare and capture.

    Clear personal documents and screens, keep people and pets out of the route, and keep lighting steady. Walk the space with the phone upright; at each spot, turn until the ring closes, and the app coaches you as you go. Tap Finish & save, then read the phone check, which lists the route checks, and review the saved photographs before leaving; those checks do not prove capture quality. After you send it, an automatic quality check assesses capture quality.

    How to walk a room

  3. Send, then the automatic render and quality check.

    Tap Send to Veylet. Send from the app: it uploads in the background. Check your account for rendering status. Veylet builds it automatically. We’ll email you when it’s ready. An automatic quality check stops a render that cannot work, such as one where the photos or the shape of the rooms did not record; it retries once when a retry can help. Other findings about photo match, coverage, stray artefacts and walkable paths are flagged for you to check before approval. No person checks it, and recording on the phone does not create a finished walkthrough by itself. Your original stays on the iPhone. A failed capture is never counted. A correction to the same walkthrough, or a permitted whole recapture including every original room, replaces it on the same link and uses no extra walkthrough.

    What each status means

  4. Review before sharing.

    When the status says Ready for your review, open the walkthrough on your phone. Check every room, turns, doorways, floor and ceiling edges, privacy and phone navigation. Tap Approve and share, or send one consolidated list of corrections. Each accepted walkthrough counts toward the 3 included in your free month, or toward your plan’s allowance after them. Capture permission and permission to publish are separate.

  5. Share on your terms.

    Approve and share turns on the walkthrough’s link. Share the link, show its QR code or copy its embed code, from the app or your account. Viewers need no account or capture app. Anyone who receives the link can forward it. Your account shows how often each walkthrough was opened.

Your first session: one practice capture.

For every new account.

Your invitation arrives when your account is admitted. The app’s getting-started guide then takes you through sign-in, the capture lesson and the practice room, and the app unlocks real captures once your practice room passes. Installation alone does not approve you for client work.

  1. Install Veylet Capture and sign in.Use the invitation link Veylet sent you, then sign in with Apple or an email link, using the email you joined with. Check the model, free storage and camera access before you start. If the device is unsupported, stop: capture needs a supported device. Install the app and sign in.
  2. Learn the capture, then try the practice room.The capture lesson is a few short illustrated cards, with the camera off. Then practise in one small room you have permission to record: clear private items and follow the prompts until the app says Room done. Website setup and inviting your team can wait. The practice room, and how to pass it.
  3. Inspect what you saved.Read the phone check, open the saved photographs and check coverage before leaving. A saved capture is your first setup checkpoint; it is not a finished or quality-approved walkthrough. Keep the original if you need help or another attempt.
  4. Send it from the app.Tap Send to Veylet. Send from the app: it uploads in the background. Check your account for rendering status. We’ll email you when it’s ready. Veylet processes the capture automatically. The automatic quality check stops a render that cannot work; other findings are flagged for you to check before approval. Your original stays on the iPhone. Client work needs explicit production approval and agreed terms.

Stuck at sign-in or sending? Keep your capture and tell Veylet support which step stopped, the device model and app build. Do not include passwords, access codes or private images in an email. For capture availability, join the waitlist; sign in with the email you joined with.

Keep the handover simple.

Already admitted?

Use the email you joined with on both the website and capture app. Sign in, then save a space. Account creation does not grant production approval.

When the listing changes.

Turn off sharing and remove its embed when the walkthrough should stop being available; use Pause sharing instead to keep the same link for later. Turning sharing off blocks new access; it cannot erase copies already downloaded. Agree hosting dates and any archive or deletion request with Veylet support.

Before you start.

What if the first result is not usable?

An automatic quality check stops a render that cannot work; other findings are flagged for you to check before approval. If your first walkthrough isn’t listing-ready, we redo it free: the redo corrects it on the same link and uses no walkthrough, though a new capture visit is not included. Keep the originals and report the affected area. After that, we agree a correction, a permitted whole recapture including every original room or the remedy in your scope. A correction or permitted whole recapture replaces the walkthrough on the same link and uses no extra walkthrough; any other new accepted capture is its own walkthrough and link. Sharing waits for review and approval.

Can every visitor open a tour?

Visitors use a current browser with graphics support on a phone, tablet or computer. Performance depends on the tour, device and connection. Share a direct link as a fallback for website builders that block embedded content. Portal compatibility must be checked with that portal.

Can an agency use it free?

Eligible App Store subscribers receive 1 free month with 3 accepted walkthroughs in total. They begin when the plan is activated with a payment method on file, and there is one trial per agency (ABN) and workspace. The first charge is on the day they end; cancel before then and nothing is charged. App Store subscriptions renew at the price of the plan you chose, monthly or annual, unless cancelled through Apple. Invoiced service continues only under explicitly agreed and settled terms; it does not auto-renew. On the monthly Veylet plan each paid month includes 3 accepted walkthroughs, the same as the free month, and unused ones roll over, up to 6 banked; the annual plan has 36 to use any time in the plan year. For a busier month the account owner can add a pack of 3 or 10 walkthroughs, valid 12 months, including during the free months. Check the renewal date on your account; you can cancel any time. Every walkthrough you released stays live while your plan runs; when it ends, its links keep working for 14 days, then go offline until you restart it. While capture quality is still being proven we onboard accounts in cohorts, so ask about availability before promising a client a date.

Is a walkthrough a measured survey?

No. It provides visual context for a space. It is not a measured floor plan, building survey or guarantee of condition. Keep listing photography and required property information available alongside it.
